title: End-to-End Fidelity Validation Lab Manual — Runtime Benchmarking & Observability
author: Maya K. Ortega
body:
Summary
-------
This lab manual defines a repeatable, end-to-end validation workflow for runtime fidelity, cost and observability when making changes to serving kernel scheduling, quantization profiles, routing/fallback policies, and telemetry enrichment. The manual is intended for SREs, runtime engineers, and performance QA engineers who need deterministic validation before rollouts to Dedicated/Hosted fleets.

Scope
-----
- Controlled lab and CI testbed exercises covering: kernel scheduler changes, model-variant swaps, quantization profile updates, eviction and warmstart behavior, routing fallback correctness, and telemetry/enrichment validation.
- Focus on observable fidelity (semantic quality), SLO preservation (P99 latency, error rate), and telemetry completeness (span coverage, attribute set).
- Excludes upstream model training or dataset curation; assumes validated model weights.

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
----------------------------
- No observable regression in defined prompt suite: prompt-set pass-rate >= 98% (see Acceptance Checklist).
- Latency SLOs preserved: P50 < 60ms, P95 < 120ms, P99 < 300ms for the configured test shape.
- Telemetry signal completeness: 100% of major request traces contain kernel-orchestrator span + kv-cache span + dispatch-daemon span.
- Automated detection of fidelity regressions via diff-based eval and embedding-similarity thresholds.

Testbed Topology (text diagram)
-------------------------------
Lab cluster (isolated VPC) topology:
- traffic-generator -> runtime-gw (ingress proxy) -> router -> dispatch-daemon -> kernel-orchestrator -> GPU-pool / CPU-fallback nodes
- auxiliary services: kv-cache-service, eviction-controller, telemetry-bridge, metrics-exporter, trace-collector

Required services and minimum versions
-------------------------------------
| Service                | Min version | Purpose                                | Owner |
|------------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| runtime-gw             | 2.4.0       | Ingress routing, rate shaping          | eng-platform |
| kernel-orchestrator    | 1.8.2       | Kernel selection & scheduling          | serving-runtime |
| dispatch-daemon        | 3.1.0       | Request fanout & concurrency shaping   | serving-runtime |
| kv-cache-service       | 0.9.5       | Prefix/KV caching & warmstart hints    | eng-platform |
| eviction-controller    | 1.2.0       | Cross-tenant eviction coordination     | eng-sre |
| telemetry-bridge       | 2.2.0       | Enrich and forward traces/metrics      | eng-platform |
| trace-collector (jaeger)| 1.31.0     | Trace capture for E2E correlation      | eng-sre |

Baseline artifacts
------------------
- Golden prompt-suite: /data/lab/golden-prompt-suite-2026.json (1000 prompts across short/medium/long sequences).
- Golden embeddings snapshot: /artifacts/golden-embeddings-2026.tar.gz (used for semantic diff checks).
- Baseline kernel metric snapshot: s3://redwood-perf/baseline/kernel-metrics-2026-02-01.json

Benchmarks and Metrics to Capture
--------------------------------
- Latencies: P50, P90, P95, P99, tail-99.9 (end-to-end and kernel-only).
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec under shaped arrival processes.
- Resource signals: GPU utilization, GPU-memory fragmentation, CPU steal, NIC TX/RX.
- Fidelity: embedding cosine similarity, BLEU-like sequence similarity for deterministic prompts, classification/QA exact match for labeled prompts.
- Observability coverage: % traces with required spans, % requests with sampling_id, % logs with request_id.

Testing Workflows (high-level)
------------------------------
1) Preflight: environment sanity
   - Verify service versions and config (see config-check CLI below).
   - Start trace-collector and telemetry-bridge in debug mode.
2) Baseline capture
   - Run golden prompt-suite against the baseline runtime configuration, store traces/metrics/artifacts.
3) Change under test
   - Apply kernel scheduling change / quantization profile / routing update in isolated test namespace.
4) Controlled replay
   - Replay captured traffic shapes (steady-state, microburst, heavy-tail) and run golden prompt-suite concurrently.
5) Automated fidelity checks
   - Run embedding-similarity diff and per-prompt regression detector.
6) Observability validation
   - Check trace/span coverage and metric cardinality including enriched attributes.
7) Acceptance gating
   - Apply acceptance checklist and sign-off for canary.

Detailed Procedures
-------------------
A. Kernel scheduler change validation (engineer-run)
1. Coordinate with owner and schedule lab window; tag change PR with {lab-validation-needed}.
2. Snapshot baseline artifacts (metrics, traces, outputs).
3. Deploy planner branch to kernel-orchestrator in test namespace: kubectl set image ... --record.
4. Warmstart KV cache hinting: pre-warm top 20 prefixes from golden prompt-suite.
5. Run three workload shapes: steady (r=500 rps), burst (3x for 30s every 5min), tail-heavy (Pareto shape).
6. Capture traces (100% sampling) and metrics at 1s resolution.
7. Run regression detector: python tools/regression_detector.py --baseline s3://... --candidate ./artifacts/candidate-output.json
8. If embedding similarity drop > 0.07 average or > 10 prompts below threshold, abort and file incident.
9. If performance SLOs violated (P99 > 1.5x baseline), revert change and open ticket.

B. Quantization profile update validation (automated pipeline)
1. Pipeline triggers from quantization-profile PR.
2. Build candidate artifacts and deploy to canary pool of 10 GPUs.
3. Run golden prompt-suite with deterministic seeds; capture outputs.
4. Run automatic semantic check: cosine similarity on embeddings (thresholds in acceptance checklist).
5. If any prompt in labeled set loses exact match or similarity below threshold, mark profile as failing.

C. Eviction and warmstart behavior (chaos-style)
1. Start a long-run session workload for warm KV cache builds.
2. Trigger eviction-controller to evict a tenant shard and observe eviction propagation.
3. Verify warmstart hints cause cache warm-up within 60s and P95 latency returns to baseline within 120s.
4. Validate no request leaks or auth errors during handoff.

CLI and Example Commands
------------------------
- Config check: ./tools/lab_config_check.sh --env lab --services runtime-gw,kernel-orchestrator,dispatch-daemon
- Start traffic generator: ./tools/traffic_gen --shape steady --rps 500 --duration 20m --out ./runs/steady-2026-03-01
- Run regression detector: python tools/regression_detector.py --baseline s3://redwood-perf/baseline --candidate ./runs/steady-2026-03-01/outputs.json --report ./runs/report.json

Example config snippet (YAML)
---------------------------
run_id: e2e-lab-2026-03-05
workload_shapes:
  - name: steady
    rps: 500
    duration: 20m
  - name: burst
    rps_profile: "spike:3x:30s:period:5m"
sampling:
  traces: 100%
  metrics_resolution: 1s
fidelity_checks:
  embedding_similarity_threshold: 0.85
  labeled_prompt_exact_match: 0.98

Acceptance checklist (must pass all)
-----------------------------------
- [ ] Regression detector: overall pass (no more than 2% prompts flagged).
- [ ] Latency SLOs: P50/P95/P99 within defined thresholds.
- [ ] Observability: required spans present in >= 99.5% of traces.
- [ ] Resource safety: no GPU memory OOMs; fragmentation delta < 5% vs baseline.
- [ ] No functional errors (auth, 5xx, malformed outputs) above 0.1%.

Signal artifacts and retention
----------------------------
- Traces and metrics for each run stored under s3://redwood-lab-runs/{run_id}/ with retention 90 days.
- Output diffs and reports under artifacts/ in the CI workspace; retain for 30 days.

Failure modes and escalation
---------------------------
- Fidelity regression detected: open a regression ticket (label: perf+fidelity) and notify author + eng-sre.
- SLO breach during lab run: pause test, capture extended traces, and create an incident with severity P2 if breach persists > 15m.
- Observability gap: escalate to eng-platform to verify telemetry-bridge configuration and collector health.

Runbook links and ownership
--------------------------
- Kernel scheduler owner: serving-runtime (oncall alias: #srv-runtime-oncall).
- Eviction-controller owner: eng-sre (alias: #eng-sre).
- Telemetry ingestion owner: eng-platform (alias: #observability).
- Related runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-deployment-circuit-breakers-and-sla-fallback-playbook-2026

Automation and CI integration
----------------------------
- Recommended: run quantization-profile and small-sample fidelity checks as part of PR gating (fast-path). Full golden-suite runs scheduled nightly or on-demand via the lab pipeline.
- CI artifacts MUST include run_id, git-commit, kernel-orchestrator-image, and quantization-profile-id for traceability.

Appendix: Quick cheat-sheet
--------------------------
- Quick start: tools/lab_bootstrap.sh --run e2e-lab --env lab
- Baseline artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/baseline/
- Who to call: serving-runtime owners (Maya Ortega), eng-sre lead (Leah Thompson), telemetry (Arjun Patel).

Notes and future work
---------------------
- Add synthetic adversarial prompt generator for corner-case fidelity checks (Q3 2026).
- Integrate a lightweight human-in-the-loop review for ambiguous prompt diffs.
- Expand telemetry enrichment assertions to include token-level attributions.
